scenarios.text: Kernel selftest of the fade curve: a roofed tag holds full opacity for about the first four-fifths of its weather days, then fades visibly to nothing; the same tag unroofed runs the same shape over fewer days; a permanent memorial stays at full opacity at any age.
scenarios.expect: accept: crisp most of its life, visible fade before it goes, sooner outdoors, permanent never fades

scenarios.text: The fade curve starts dimming a fresh mark the tick it is placed and falls in a straight line to zero over its weather days, the same length whether the wall is roofed or not.
scenarios.expect: reject: fade starts at placement and roofed equals unroofed, both named false passes

scenarios.text: One colonist paints a vandal scrawl and a tally side by side at Poor, Normal and Excellent craft; at each craft the scrawl looks rougher at 64 px and its inspect pane shows lower beauty than the tally.
scenarios.expect: accept: picture and stat agree, the same hand's scrawl inspects uglier at every craft

scenarios.text: The scrawl's def has a lower base beauty than the tally's, but when one Excellent-craft colonist paints both, the two inspect at the same beauty and an unlabelled judge picks the scrawl as uglier only by its picture.
scenarios.expect: reject: the scrawl is uglier only in its def while the same hand's pair inspects alike

scenarios.text: After the six-lane spree a judge shown the walls names a throw-up, a tag, a tally, an ideoligion sigil and a scrawl, each a different shape, not one shape in different paint.
scenarios.expect: accept: several visibly different kinds, told apart as kinds

scenarios.text: All six spree lanes come out holding the same tag outline, each lane in a different tint; the def list reads six entries that share one texture.
scenarios.expect: reject: one def in six tints is a recolour, not variety

scenarios.text: A colonist walks past one mockery of them every hour for two in-game days; the mood thought from that mark is set on the first pass and refreshed once on day two, and the opinion of the painter drops only on that first pass.
scenarios.expect: accept: refreshed at most once per in-game day, opinion changed once

scenarios.text: A colonist passes the same mockery every hour; each pass resets that thought's duration, so it never expires, and the opinion of the painter drops a little more on each pass.
scenarios.expect: reject: refreshed every pass rather than at most daily, and opinion keeps moving

scenarios.text: A lived-in colony of six runs three in-game weeks unforced; most days the mood panes show no graffiti thought or one small one that expires, and the week's log holds a handful of Graffiti messages and letters.
scenarios.expect: accept: occasional stories, no colonist's mood ruled by marks, few messages per week

scenarios.text: After one week of an ordinary unforced colony every colonist holds three or four stacked graffiti debuffs from old scrawls that renew faster than they expire, and a Graffiti message fires every few hours.
scenarios.expect: reject: a standing mood tax and a message stream

scenarios.text: A colonist paints Tag_A on a wall cell, then a rival faction raider paints ThrowUp_A on the same cell; the cell then holds exactly one mark, ThrowUp_A of the rival faction, and the tag is gone.
scenarios.expect: accept: the enemy throw-up went over the tag, which is gone

scenarios.text: A raider paints a throw-up on a cell that already carries a colonist's tag; both are drawn, the throw-up layered over the tag, and inspecting the cell lists two graffiti marks.
scenarios.expect: reject: going-over stacks two marks on one cell

scenarios.text: An enemy throw-up goes over a colonist's tag, which disappears from view; when a cleaner later scrubs the throw-up, the colonist's original tag shows again on that cell.
scenarios.expect: reject: the colonist's tag survived under the throw-up instead of being gone

scenarios.text: Six colonists each finish a forced painting spree; the job log lists every paint job as completed, yet the wall lanes beside them hold no marks at all.
scenarios.expect: reject: paint jobs complete and place nothing

scenarios.text: The 64 px gallery shows every def and every random variant face-on along a lit wall; one variant of the scratch mark comes out as a faint grey speck of a few pixels.
scenarios.expect: reject: a variant that is a few pixels at play zoom reads as nothing

scenarios.text: In a close-up of a painted lane, each mark sits on the front face of the wall north of the painter's cell and runs over the crease onto the wall top; a cell whose only wall is south of it gets no mark from a paint order.
scenarios.expect: accept: on the front face over the crease, and no paint on a far side

scenarios.text: A colonist standing beside a wall seen edge-on paints there, and the mark appears as a thin decal turned along the wall top's edge strip.
scenarios.expect: reject: a mark turned along an edge-on wall passes as painted but an edge-on wall takes no paint

scenarios.text: A colonist of an ideoligion with a red flame icon paints a sigil; on the wall it shows that flame icon tinted in the ideoligion's red inside a halo frame.
scenarios.expect: accept: the ideoligion's own icon, tinted, in a frame

scenarios.text: Among the gallery's vandal marks one variant is a yellow triangle with a black lightning bolt, kept as a punk mark.
scenarios.expect: reject: a hazard-bolt sign is real-world signage, not punk graffiti

scenarios.text: At 64 px a tag variant looks like loose lettering, but on its close-up page the letters clearly read TARTE.
scenarios.expect: reject: a third-party tag legible in close-up, English only shown when zoomed in still fails

scenarios.text: Placed beside vanilla dirt filth at 64 px, a scratch mark cannot be picked out by a judge, and the build is passed because the scratch's def is labelled graffiti.
scenarios.expect: reject: a mark indistinguishable from filth accepted on its def name

scenarios.text: An art-16 colonist paints a mockery of a rival; the rival's mood pane shows one small net thought where the anger and the beauty pleasure have cancelled.
scenarios.expect: reject: a skilled slander must anger and please at once, not net to one thought

scenarios.text: A colonist with low joy and free time next to a wall takes the paint recreation job, joy rises while painting, and afterwards the colonist holds a small maker mood buff.
scenarios.expect: accept: painting is recreation that fills joy and the maker gets a buff

scenarios.text: A feuding colonist paints a mark ridiculing the other; the mark records the subject, the subject gets a hurt thought and a lower opinion of the painter, and the subject's rival gets an amused thought.
scenarios.expect: accept: names someone, hurts and amuses the right people, changes regard of the painter

scenarios.text: A colonist who never met the dead pawn paints a memorial to them, and nobody's grief changes.
scenarios.expect: reject: a memorial must come from a grieving colonist and ease that grief

scenarios.text: A message says the subject's friend defaced a mockery and the mark turns crossed out, but no pawn ever walked to that wall.
scenarios.expect: reject: the answer is logged and the mark changes with no pawn at it

scenarios.text: A cleaner with no orders walks the wall and scrubs an enemy faction's devotional sigil along with the enemy vandal tag beside it.
scenarios.expect: reject: auto-clean wipes a devotional mark

scenarios.text: The player designates three cells for Tag_B, ThrowUp_A and a tally; one colonist paints exactly those three marks on those cells and no designation is left pending.
scenarios.expect: accept: exactly the ordered marks, none pending

scenarios.text: Raiders tag the outer walls while they are still assaulting, before they ever turn to leave.
scenarios.expect: reject: tags appear on the way in rather than only on the way out

scenarios.text: Faction A left exit marks and faction B none; a letter naming A arrives and opening it jumps the camera to A's mark on the wall, A's next raid has more points than B's at the same storyteller points, and after the last A mark is scrubbed A's next raid matches B's.
scenarios.expect: accept: letter names and points at the mark, bigger raid while it stands, push lifts when gone

scenarios.text: A trader caravan passes a wall insulting its faction six times during one visit; goodwill drops once on the first pass and not again for the rest of the visit.
scenarios.expect: accept: one goodwill change per visit, never recharged

scenarios.text: The subject of a feud mockery is drafted in position; on seeing the mark the subject leaves the drafted spot to confront the painter.
scenarios.expect: reject: a drafted pawn leaves to fight

scenarios.text: A psychopath passes a crude scrawl and gets a -1 thought while an ordinary viewer gets -3.
scenarios.expect: reject: the psychopath must hold no mark thought, not a smaller one

scenarios.text: With the raid tagging switch turned off in mod settings, a raid that leaves still paints its faction's tags on the outer walls.
scenarios.expect: reject: a switched-off setting still tags

scenarios.text: A painted wall cell is deconstructed and its mark is gone the same tick; a mark on the untouched neighbouring wall stays.
scenarios.expect: accept: paint dies with its wall and only its wall

scenarios.text: On the lived-in save the raid then trader order costs one insult goodwill drop and gives one pressure letter; reloaded and run trader first, the trader's goodwill drops twice and no pressure letter arrives.
scenarios.expect: reject: the order of raid and trader changes the outcome

scenarios.text: A freshly painted tag starts losing opacity on its first day and thins steadily, day by day, until it is gone after its weather days. Marks outdoors disappear well before marks under a roof, and a permanent mark never fades.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'fade starts at placement' (the mark must stay crisp most of its life before it visibly fades)

scenarios.text: Every ordinary mark stays crisp for about ten days, then visibly fades over its last two days and vanishes. A tag in the open courtyard and a tag in the roofed dining room, painted the same hour, vanish on the same day.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'roofed and unroofed last the same' (it must go sooner outdoors)

scenarios.text: At play zoom the vandal scrawl is clearly a messy smear beside a neat tally, and the scrawl's def lists a lower base beauty. But when one colonist paints both at the same craft level, the inspect pane shows the same beauty for each.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'the scrawl is uglier only in its def, while the same hand's scrawl and tally inspect alike'

scenarios.text: A scrawl and a tally by the same painter sit side by side; the scrawl inspects at -4 beauty and the tally at -1. At 64 px the two are drawn with the same tidy, even strokes, and a viewer can't tell which is the uglier one.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'the two marks look alike and only the stat differs'

scenarios.text: After the spree, the six painters' lanes each hold a throw-up in a different colour scheme (red, teal, gold, violet, lime and white), so the wall looks colourful and varied. Each one is the same bubble-letter shape.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'one def in six tints' / red 'pool collapses to one def or one variant'

scenarios.text: A colonist walks past the same mockery every hour for two days. Their mood list shows one thought from it that refreshes once per day, but their opinion of the painter drops by another point every time they pass.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'opinion keeps moving each pass' (opinion changes once, on the first read)

scenarios.text: A colonist passes one mockery hourly. Each pass in the same day adds another copy of its mood thought, up to a cap of three, and the opinion of the painter changed only on the first pass.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'the thought stacks per pass' (the mood effect comes at most once per day)

scenarios.text: An ordinary lived-in colony of six runs four in-game days at top speed with no forcing. Over that time graffiti produced two short stories, one notice, and no standing mood penalty on anyone.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'the run is too short to reach a steady state' (the scene is three in-game weeks)

scenarios.text: Over three in-game weeks of an ordinary colony of six, the tester counts Graffiti letters and finds only three, with no mood ruled by marks. The blue top-left notices from painting and scrubbing were not counted.
scenarios.expect: reject: false_pass 'messages are counted only for one kind'

scenarios.text: Over a long game, ordinary tags fade and disappear while one mark flagged permanent stays fully crisp on the wall for an in-game year without ever fading.
scenarios.expect: accept: the leaf exempts permanent marks ('unless it is permanent'; oracle 'permanent never fades'), and ordinary marks still weather
